title: Circular Multi-Sensor Motor Encoder Ring
description: The split between what BRIEF.md fixes and what it leaves open. Every fixed_requirements entry carries the verbatim brief text that substantiates it, bound to the recorded brief digest. An open_decisions entry is a choice for the design agent: record it in 'chosen' with 'rationale', and never move it into fixed_requirements. Missing details are design freedom, not permission to fabricate unstated user requirements.

brief.authority: supplied by the benchmark; authoritative; preserved byte for byte and never edited

derivation.method: BRIEF.md was read and split; no design decision was taken. Every fixed_requirements entry, and every spec-table row sourced from the brief, carries a quotation that was checked by literal substring match against the brief bytes digested above. The build refuses to emit this file if any quotation is not found.
derivation.where_the_quotations_are: Every one of them is in this file: fixed_requirements[].brief_evidence and brief_spec_rows[].brief_evidence. The count above is the sum of those two lists, so it is recomputable from this repository alone - re-read BRIEF.md and check each string is a substring of it. brief_spec_rows carries the quotations behind the README's spec table, which would otherwise cite the brief with the evidence left in a build script.
derivation.review: two rounds of adversarial review against the brief, looking for invented requirements, lost requirements, evidence supporting a weaker claim than the one made beside it, and worksheet questions that presuppose their own answer

open_decisions.decision: Whether the sensing technology is magnetic or optical.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief offers the two as an explicit either/or ("magnetic or optical sensors") and does not pick one; the choice drives sensor orientation, the rotor-side target, and the whole placement geometry.

open_decisions.decision: Which specific sensor device is used — package, output type (analog, digital, incremental, absolute), interface, and supply rail.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names no part, vendor, or interface for the sensing elements; it fixes only their number, spacing, radius discipline and technology family.

open_decisions.decision: The actual sensing radius (and therefore the sensor pitch circle diameter).
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires a "precise common radius" and bounds the annulus with an ~90 mm outer diameter and a ≥40 mm central keep-out, but never states the radius itself.

open_decisions.decision: MCU selection: family, core, package, pin count, clocking, and how many sensor channels it must terminate directly.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief says only "a small MCU" and names no device, architecture, or vendor.

open_decisions.decision: Which host link is implemented — CAN or differential serial (or both) — and which transceiver/PHY realises it.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief gives the two as alternatives and names no transceiver, connector, data rate, or protocol layer.

open_decisions.decision: Sensor aggregation topology: point-to-point to the MCU, a shared bus, multiplexing, daisy-chaining, or a mixture.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states only that the MCU "collects the sensors"; it is silent on how the 12 channels reach it, which is the decision that determines whether radial routing can stay symmetric.

open_decisions.decision: Power architecture below the 12 V input: linear vs switching, number and value of rails, sequencing, and how sensor supplies are decoupled or separated from digital supplies.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief fixes the input voltage and that regulation is local, and nothing else about topology, rail voltages, or current budget.

open_decisions.decision: Connector selection: how many connectors, type, pin count, orientation, mating direction, and retention.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief fixes only that connectors sit on the outer perimeter; no part, pin count, or cable interface is named.

open_decisions.decision: Protection strategy for the 12 V input and the communications bus — reverse polarity, overvoltage/transient, overcurrent, and ESD.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief is silent on protection entirely; the motor-adjacent, 12 V, cable-connected context is a stressor to be addressed, not a specified circuit.

open_decisions.decision: Stackup: final layer count, copper weights, dielectric materials, finished thickness, and surface finish.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states no stackup; the metadata's "likely layer count: 4" is a benchmark expectation, not a stated user requirement.

open_decisions.decision: Exact annulus geometry: the inner diameter actually used above the 40 mm minimum, whether the centre is a true routed cutout or a keep-out on solid board, and edge/cutout tolerance callouts.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief gives a minimum keep-out diameter and refers to a "central opening/cutout" without fixing which form it takes or how tightly it is toleranced.

open_decisions.decision: Mechanical mounting: number, size and bolt-circle of mounting holes, fastener and standoff scheme, and any angular indexing/keying feature that registers the ring to the motor.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief says the board mounts concentrically around the shaft but specifies no mounting hardware, hole pattern, or angular registration feature.

open_decisions.decision: Assembly sidedness: single- or double-sided placement, and which side faces the rotor target.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief does not state which face of the ring is the sensing face or whether the back side may carry parts.

open_decisions.decision: How an angular zero/index is established — whether any index mark, reference sensor, or startup calibration exists.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires position reporting from 12 evenly spaced sensors but says nothing about absolute reference, homing, or index.

open_decisions.decision: The rotor-side interface: target magnet ring, code wheel or equivalent, its pole/line count, and the target air gap.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief describes only the PCB side of the system; the moving target and the mechanical gap it presents are not specified.

open_decisions.decision: Position resolution, update rate, latency, and the on-wire message format and node addressing over the chosen link.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names the transport as CAN or differential serial but fixes no performance figure, protocol, framing, or address scheme.

open_decisions.decision: Grounding and return strategy for a ring whose centre must stay free of copper — how continuous return paths are maintained under 12 sets of radial traces, and whether sensor and power returns are partitioned.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief is silent on grounding; it only requires the central opening/cutout to be kept free of copper as required, which is what makes the return path a genuine design problem.

open_decisions.decision: Bus electrical details: whether this node carries termination, whether it is bus-powered or separately powered, and stub/branch handling on the perimeter connectors.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief mentions CAN or differential serial and a 12 V input but does not say how the node sits on the bus or whether power and data share a connector.

open_decisions.decision: Environmental and operating envelope: temperature range, vibration, ingress, and the magnetic/EMI environment near the motor.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states no environmental conditions, ratings, or qualification requirements.

open_decisions.decision: Fabrication and assembly vendor and the process capability class targeted (minimum trace/space, minimum hole, internal cutout routing, placement positional and rotational accuracy).
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names no fabricator, process, or tolerance class, yet the "precise common radius" requirement can only be defended against a specific stated capability.
